paper.title: Inspiration booster or creative fixation? The dual mechanisms of LLMs in shaping individual creativity in tasks of different complexity
paper.pdf_filename: Cheng et al (2025) - Inspiration booster or creative fixation.pdf
paper.version_read: Journal version of record: Xusen Cheng and Lulu Zhang, Humanities and Social Sciences Communications (2025) 12:1563, DOI 10.1057/s41599-025-05867-9 (PDF p. 1 and page footers).
paper.one_line_finding: With 204 people analyzed per experiment, an LLM partner posting ERNIE Bot ideas raised expert-rated creativity over a scripted human partner on the simple task (2.549 vs 2.182, F(1,200) = 17.152, P < 0.001) and scored lower on the complex task (2.351 vs 2.441, F(1,200) = 1.021, printed with P = 0.028), while two ideas per response instead of ten raised complex-task creativity (2.520 vs 2.139) and lowered simple-task creativity (2.171 vs 2.466) (pp. 5 and 7).

estimates.outcome: Expert-rated creativity of the participant's ideas (overall novelty and usefulness), both task complexities pooled
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Two trained independent external experts, blind to participant demographics, hypotheses and experimental design, rated each idea on overall novelty and usefulness using a five-point scale from extremely low to extremely high. Their average was used as the overall creativity score for each participant's ideas (PDF p. 5, Measurements).

estimates.control_arm: Human partner, simple task and Human partner, complex task (combined)

estimates.notes: This is the expert-rated output outcome despite its position under the Self-reported creativity heading. The paper lists human before LLM; the negative t and d retain that human-minus-LLM orientation, opposite to this record’s treatment/control order. No sign has been reversed and no mean difference computed. The confidence interval is printed beside these results without an identified estimand; it does not contain the printed d. Retain ci_of=null and do not assign these bounds to paper_effect or to a raw difference. The standardizer for d is unspecified. The one-way and factorial partner main-effect ANOVAs are alternate analyses of the same full-sample outcome and contrast, documented in resolutions and not_extracted rather than separate estimates. Arm counts and explicit standard errors are absent from the saved article. Task-specific simple effects are moderation results excluded by rule 5. Supplement update: the pooled participant counts are now transcribed from the demographic-table note, with a source quote above. The individual task-cell counts and explicit standard errors for this original pooled test remain unreported. The supplement does not identify this confidence interval or the standardizer for d. The mediator-adjusted direct regression is recorded separately as s1_creativity_llm_vs_human_pooled_direct_adjusted; its coefficient and standard error are not statistics for this t-test.

estimates.notes: Full-sample response-type main effect from the factorial ANOVA crossing response type with task complexity. The proposed constrained-responsive configuration is treatment and batch-responsive is control. The schema’s eta2 type contains the paper’s partial eta squared. F and partial eta squared are unsigned; no pooled arm means or signed coefficient is printed, so the direction is unknown. No pooled SDs, arm counts, standard errors or confidence interval for a signed contrast are printed. Task-specific means and dispersions are not averaged or substituted into this record. Task-specific simple effects are moderation results excluded by rule 5. Supplement update: the pooled participant counts are now transcribed from the demographic-table note, with a source quote above. The other missing pooled descriptives and uncertainty for this original factorial contrast remain unreported. The mediator-adjusted direct regression is recorded separately as s2_creativity_constrained_vs_batch_pooled_direct_adjusted; it does not supply a signed total effect for this ANOVA.

open_items: Randomized and analyzed counts for the individual task-by-treatment cells remain unreported. Supplement 41599_2025_5867_MOESM1_ESM.pdf, PDF p. 10 (printed p. 9), Table S5, and PDF p. 11, Table S6, state only the pooled treatment/comparison group counts, now sourced in the estimates. Cell counts are not inferred from those totals, demographic probabilities, degrees of freedom or equal-allocation assumptions.

The estimand of the confidence interval accompanying the pooled expert-creativity comparison in S1 is not identified. Its bounds do not contain the printed d. ci_of remains null, and the bounds are not used as an interval for d. The standardizer for the printed d is also unspecified (PDF p. 5).

S2 still has no printed pooled arm means, pooled participant SDs, signed total-effect contrast, or explicit uncertainty for a signed total effect; the factorial F statistic and partial eta squared do not establish its direction (main PDF p. 6). The pooled arm counts are now settled by Supplement 41599_2025_5867_MOESM1_ESM.pdf, PDF p. 11, Table S6. Its Table S8 on PDF p. 12 supplies a mediator-adjusted direct coefficient and SE, recorded separately, which do not settle the missing total-effect direction or descriptives.

Overlap between participants in S1 and S2 is unknown. The paper does not say that recruitment was separate or that prior participants were excluded. No combined unique-person total is inferred. The screening sample_overlap field names no other paper sharing this sample (PDF pp. 4-5).

ERNIE Bot version and release year are not stated; ai_tool.year is null. Participant country and recruitment channel are not stated. The Chinese-language context described in the Discussion does not confirm the country of recruitment (PDF pp. 3-5 and 8).

The excluded conditional creativity analyses have unresolved dispersion labels and possible decimal errors; figure captions label the error bars as standard errors while the text labels the cell dispersions as SDs. S1 also has an inconsistent complex-task test. These numbers have not been corrected or substituted into pooled outcomes (PDF pp. 5-7).

The excluded S2 fixation moderated-mediation index still has a sign/description conflict and repeats the S1 index. The reference ideas used to score fixation in the human-partner arms also remain unclear. The supplement does not resolve either issue.

Supplement 41599_2025_5867_MOESM1_ESM.pdf, PDF p. 12 (unnumbered), Tables S7-S8, Model 4, labels the coefficients beta without identifying whether the regression outcome is raw or standardized. The new regression outcome_scale fields remain null. The supplement gives experiment-group counts but no model-specific total count, exact treatment p-values or treatment confidence intervals for these direct-effect equations.
